cases.title: GLS fit and full parameter covariance

provenance.sampling: No draws; supplied covariance is Cov(moment estimator), already scaled for its sample.
provenance.transformations: Identity; fit intercept and slope with a correlated four-moment target.
provenance.limitations: Checks linear optimal weighting and covariance. No empirical model identification or finite-sample coverage claim.

cases.title: Stone-Geary welfare versus independent primal optimization

provenance.sampling: No sample or survey weights. One household; two deterministic states.
provenance.transformations: Direct utility maximization and four expenditure minimizations use raw log Stone-Geary utility; no puremacro welfare reference.
provenance.limitations: Independent SciPy SLSQP oracle for interior preferences. Not an empirical household calibration.

cases.title: Household incidence, expansion weights and uniform rebates

provenance.sampling: Two representative groups expand to three low-budget and one high-budget household; no sampling inference.
provenance.transformations: Cobb-Douglas exact cost indices, equal transfer per expanded household, and weighted EV totals.
provenance.limitations: Conditional static incidence with fixed preferences and exogenous prices; no empirical Mexico or general-equilibrium claim.

steady_state.unit: c,k: goods per capita; a: log technology

lagged_capital_derivative.unit: output units per unit of lagged capital

technology_derivative.unit: output units per unit log-technology innovation

provenance.sampling: No sample. Deterministic steady state and first-order derivatives at zero technology.
provenance.transformations: k' = alpha*beta*exp(a)*k**alpha; c = (1-alpha*beta)*exp(a)*k**alpha. Variable order c,k,a.
provenance.limitations: Checks this special log-utility, Cobb-Douglas, full-depreciation case and its local derivatives only.

provenance.sampling: 2,500 common Gaussian innovations from NumPy default_rng(20260920); discard first 500. Covariance uses ddof=1; lag-1 covariance uses separately centered endpoints and N-2.
provenance.transformations: Match variable/state/shock labels; unfold derivative tensors without factorial rescaling; add deterministic steady state to simulated deviations. Validate model, innovations and reference checksums.
provenance.limitations: External-software agreement for one small model at order two, conditional on supplied innovations. No live Dynare run, population-moment accuracy or published empirical replication is claimed.

cases.title: Observed ENIGH decile baskets reproduce official national totals

data.origin: INEGI ENIGH 2024 national household income deciles; Cuadros 3.2 and 4.2
data.reference_origin: literal national published totals, not the derived CSV

provenance.sampling: Ten national household income deciles; expansion counts include all households. No sampling covariance is available.
provenance.transformations: Published thousands of MXN multiplied by 1000; decile totals divided by all-household counts. Eight consumption categories plus outward transfers equal monetary expenditure. CSV decimal rounding motivates the tolerance.
provenance.limitations: Validates the extraction, weights, units and selected accounting totals of actual survey aggregates. Does not replicate an empirical causal model, identify tariff responses or validate within-decile heterogeneity.

coefficients.unit: GDP growth percentage points; intercept or per one-percent-of-GDP tax increase

irf.unit: GDP log-percent per one-percent-of-GDP tax increase

data.origin: Romer and Romer (2010) original author archive

provenance.sampling: 1950Q1–2007Q4, 232 quarterly observations; 14 coefficients, 218 residual degrees of freedom.
provenance.transformations: OLS of 100*delta log(real GDP) on intercept and lags 0–12 of 100*(DEFIC+LONGR)/NOMGDP; conventional residual-df OLS covariance. Cumulate tax coefficients and full covariance to obtain GDP-level responses.
provenance.limitations: Frozen independent software port of the authors' baseline specification; not a live RATS run. Numerical agreement does not establish narrative shock exogeneity or reproduce robustness specifications.

response_h10.unit: GDP log-percent per one-percent-of-GDP tax increase

data.origin: Romer and Romer (2010) original author archive

provenance.sampling: 1950Q1–2007Q4, 232 quarterly observations; 14 coefficients, 218 residual degrees of freedom.
provenance.transformations: OLS of 100*delta log(real GDP) on intercept and lags 0–12 of 100*(DEFIC+LONGR)/NOMGDP; conventional residual-df OLS covariance. Cumulate tax coefficients and full covariance to obtain GDP-level responses.
provenance.limitations: One original-data baseline result. Absolute tolerance 0.005 reflects two-decimal publication rounding; integer horizon must match exactly. The original-data t statistic misses its published rounding interval by about 0.000003925; this remains a failure, also present in the authors' RATS databanks. It is not a software-parity tolerance or independent causal validation.
